judged_text: The write `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId } })` re-derives authorization only from the earlier in-memory check with no ownership predicate in the update's where clause, and the guests are created before calendar/email work with no rollback path. Attendee rows are persisted even if eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees or email sending subsequently fails, leaving the booking's stored attendee list, the remote calendar event's attendee list, and the sent invitations permanently out of sync (added guests see the event in DB responses but were never invited or calendared).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first (`prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})`), then the handler performs side effects (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`). There is no transaction/rollback or compensating delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not caught), so attendee rows can be permanently persisted even though calendar invites/emails were not updated/sent, leaving DB vs. remote calendar/email out of sync exactly as described. (The authorization predicate-in-`where` point is weaker because an in-memory permission check exists, but the partial-failure inconsistency is directly verifiable from the diff.)
